probe_question: Can scheduled-Chat continuation safely rely on a historical Git commit/tree after every retaining ref becomes unreachable, and which zero-cost repository-native variants preserve semantic recovery without assuming undocumented GitHub retention?

official_sources.observation: git prune removes objects unreachable from refs, subject to expiry and packing rules.
git gc keeps objects referenced by branches, tags, reflogs and refs, while unreachable objects may be pruned after expiry; this is not a permanent-retention contract.

GitHub documents that rewritten commits may remain temporarily reachable through SHA/caches/PR refs, but after all references are removed server garbage collection can expunge unreachable Git objects. Therefore SHA-only access after total dereference is not a durable availability guarantee.

local_git_probe.environment: local git object database; no hosted runner, Codespaces, external API credit or paid compute

cases.setup: Create snapshot commit A, rewind the only active branch, expire reflogs immediately, run git gc --prune=now.
cases.result: A commit and its tree become unavailable to git cat-file after pruning.
cases.interpretation: A bare historical SHA is not a zero-dependency retention mechanism once every retaining ref disappears and GC is allowed.

cases.setup: Create branch retain -> A, rewind active branch, expire reflogs, run git gc --prune=now; then delete retain and prune again.
cases.result: A remains available while retain exists, then becomes unavailable after retain deletion plus GC.
cases.interpretation: A mutable branch/tag anchor converts an unreachable snapshot into a reachable one but does not survive adversarial ref deletion or total same-domain rewind.

cases.setup: Read semantic payload from A before rewind, rewind active branch, materialize the payload into a new file on a new current reachable commit, expire reflogs and prune now.
cases.result: Original A becomes unavailable, while the new reachable commit and copied semantic payload remain available.
cases.interpretation: Copying the required semantic recovery payload into the current reachable role namespace removes dependence on old-object retention for ordinary GC/rewrite cases. It preserves semantics, not original object identity.

cases.setup: Treat missing historical object as unresolved and refuse reconstruction from an unverifiable substitute.
cases.result: Safety is preserved but liveness/outcome parity is not restored.
cases.interpretation: Fail-closed handling is required but is not itself a parity-closing recovery mechanism.

retained_exact_distinct_mechanism.definition: Before relying on a snapshot that may lose its last retaining ref, materialize the minimum verified semantic recovery payload plus source hash/provenance into the currently reachable role-local namespace, exact-read it back, and treat any later missing/mismatched historical object as fail-closed rather than assuming GitHub object retention.
retained_exact_distinct_mechanism.tested_scope: Local Git rewrite/GC with immediate reflog expiry and prune-now; semantic-copy preservation under a currently reachable branch; exact GitHub hosted retention duration was not assumed or measured.
retained_exact_distinct_mechanism.remaining_failure: If the entire repository authority domain is rewound/deleted/recreated so the current semantic copy and every other monotonic witness disappear, this mechanism has no independent surviving anchor.

rejected_variant.reason: It preserves reachability only while the mutable ref remains. Deleting or rewinding every retaining ref reopens the GC-loss boundary.

exact_next_candidate: Probe a second durability domain that remains Chat-native, zero-cost and quota-independent without protected-primary/manual execution, or prove a tighter impossibility boundary. Compare same-repository pull-request refs/cached views, repository issue/comment or other non-Git durable objects if exposed within allowed write boundaries, and fail-closed dual-witness designs. Reject any route whose durability depends on undocumented cache retention, admin/support action, protected refs, paid storage/compute, or user execution.
